facts.statement: Langstonia is an extinct genus of crocodylomorph.
facts.quote: genus: Langstonia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Langstonia huilensis.
facts.quote: species: huilensis

facts.statement: The genus Langstonia was established in 2007 by Alfredo Paolillo and Omar Linares.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Paolillo & Linares, 2007

facts.statement: The species was originally described by Wann Langston Jr. in 1965.
facts.quote: authority: (Langston, 1965)

facts.statement: The name Langstonia honors the paleontologist Wann Langston Jr.
facts.quote: Langstonia (meaning "[crocodile] of Langston", in honor of paleontologist Wann Langston, Jr.)

facts.statement: Langstonia lived during the Middle Miocene, specifically the Laventan land-mammal age.
facts.quote: It lived in the middle Miocene (specifically in the Laventan land-mammal age)

facts.statement: Fossils of Langstonia have been found in the Monkey Beds of the Villavieja Formation in Colombia.
facts.quote: in the "Monkey Beds" of the Colombian Villavieja Formation

facts.statement: The first fossils were discovered in the Huila province of Colombia by geologist José Royo y Gómez.
facts.quote: The first fossils of Langstonia were discovered in the province of Huila in Colombia by the Spanish geologist José Royo y Gómez

facts.statement: These initial discoveries occurred during expeditions led by paleontologist Robert Stirton.
facts.quote: during the expeditions in the region by the American paleontologist Robert Stirton

facts.statement: The fossils were found in the Tatacoa Desert at locality V-4517.
facts.quote: They were found in the area called the Tatacoa Desert at the locality V-4517

facts.statement: The geological formation containing these fossils is known as the Monkey Beds, named in 1945.
facts.quote: These have been named the Honda Group, of the La Venta fauna, the geological formation named the "lechos de monos" (Monkey Beds) in 1945

facts.statement: Many discovered remains are housed in the Museum of Paleontology at the University of California, Berkeley.
facts.quote: Many of the remains discovered were then sent to the collections of the Museum of Paleontology at the University of California, Berkeley (UCMP)

facts.statement: Wann Langston Jr. formally described the specimens in his 1965 monograph Fossil Crocodylians from Colombia.
facts.quote: The description of the specimens did not come until 1965, when the American paleontologist Wann Langston Jr. published his monograph Fossil Crocodylians from Colombia

facts.statement: Langston designated dentary UCMP 37877 as the holotype for the species Sebecus huilensis.
facts.quote: As for the sebecid material he designated the dentary UCMP 37877 as the holotype of a new species a fragmentary taxon, which he called Sebecus huilensis

facts.statement: Langston distinguished the species by noting its dentary fragment was 68% larger than that of the Argentine species Sebecus icaeorhinus.
facts.quote: Langston gave the taxon a new species considering that besides being larger, as the dentary fragment is 68% larger than the Argentine species, S. icaeorhinus, it was also proportionally thinner

facts.statement: The species is characterized by being proportionally thinner and having more recurved, laterally compressed teeth.
facts.quote: it was also proportionally thinner, and had with more recurved teeth being laterally compressed

facts.statement: Arthur Busbey reported new remains of the species from the Monkey Beds in 1986.
facts.quote: Arthur Busbey (1986) later brought new remains of the species also from the "Monkey Beds" of Huila in Colombia

facts.statement: Busbey described the first known remains of a jugal bone, jaw joints, and an osteoderm for this family.
facts.quote: He also described the first remains of the jugal bone, the suspensory and retroarticular joint in the jaw, and a fragment of bone scute (osteoderm), which were the earliest known for this family

facts.statement: New remains were reported by Langston and Zulma Gasparini in 1997.
facts.quote: Langston, along with the Argentine paleontologist Zulma Gasparini, reported new remains of the species in a contribution on fossil crocodylomorphs of Colombia for the book Vertebrate Paleontology of the Neotropics: The Miocene Fauna of La Venta (1997)

facts.statement: A flattened tooth from the Middle Miocene found in the Fitzcarrald Arch of Peru has been assigned to Langstonia.
facts.quote: in the area of the Peruvian Amazon known as the Fitzcarrald Arch has been found a characteristically flattened tooth from the middle Miocene therefore assigned to Langstonia

facts.statement: Fragments from the Middle Paleocene Itaboraí Basin in Brazil are classified as related to this species.
facts.quote: a premaxilla and maxilla fragment found in Itaboraí Basin in Brazil dating from the Middle Paleocene (and where have been found fossils of other sebecids) has been classified as related to this species, under the name of Sebecus cf. huilensis

facts.statement: Paolillo and Linares reassigned a previously attributed Peruvian fossil to the genus Barinasuchus.
facts.quote: Paolillo and Linares also clarified the status of the Peruvian fossil before assigned to the species, assigning it to Barinasuchus

facts.statement: Some authors still debate whether the species should remain within the genus Sebecus.
facts.quote: although some authors still maintain both species within Sebecus

facts.statement: Additional fragments were recovered in 1976 at the Monkey Pod locality by Dr. Ernest Lundelius Jr.
facts.quote: These fragments were recovered in 1976 in the "Monkey Pod" locality of La Venta (Baraya Member of the Villavieja Formation) by Dr Lundelius Ernest Jr.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Langstonia was found in the Duke 57 locality within the Villavieja Formation and includes a right premaxilla, part of a maxilla, a tooth, a rostrum fragment, and two vertebrae.
facts.quote: Found in the Duke 57 locality in Villavieja Formation; consists of a right premaxilla and part of the maxilla, the front left tooth, part of the dorsal border of a rostrum and two vertebrae.

facts.statement: The premaxilla of the type specimen measures 12.8 cm in length and is described as tall and thin with fine grooves on its outer surface.
facts.quote: The premaxillary measured 12.8 cm in length, is tall and thin compared to the S. icaeorhinus being covered with fine grooves on its outer surface.

facts.statement: The premaxilla contains three dental alveoli, with the fourth tooth being particularly enlarged at twice the size of the third, while the first two teeth are small.
facts.quote: It has three dental alveoli in the premaxilla, from the edge of the second tooth to the fourth, which is particularly enlarged, being twice the third (reverse that in S. icaeorhinus), while the first two teeth should be small.

facts.statement: A diastema following the fourth premaxillary tooth accommodated a lower tooth that exceeded 3.5 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: After the fourth premaxillary tooth there is a space or diastema in that fitted the fourth lower tooth that exceeded the 3.5 centimeters

facts.statement: The dentary bone is high and features four sockets, with the third and fourth being straight and the fourth being the largest.
facts.quote: The dentary is high, with four sockets, two projecting forward and a third and fourth straight, the latter being the largest.

facts.statement: A single tooth found in the Inuya and Mapuya localities of the Amazon region in Peru is indistinguishable in size and shape from Langstonia huilensis.
facts.quote: MUSM 912: A single tooth found in the area of Fitzcarrald Arch in the localities of Inuya and Mapuya in the Amazon region of Peru; its size and shape are indistinguishable from L. huilensis.

facts.statement: Langstonia teeth are zyphodont with very flattened sides, slightly curved backs, serrated edges containing 5-6 denticles per millimeter, and no grooves on their surface.
facts.quote: Teeth are of the zyphodont kind, with very flattened sides, slightly curved back and with serrated edges with small denticles (between 5-6 denticles per millimeter in the teeth of this genus) and also without any grooves on its surface.

facts.statement: Langstonia possessed elongated limbs and a stiff back, adaptations ideal for running and supporting its weight on land.
facts.quote: these crocodylomorphs also had more elongated limbs, stiff back, ideal to hold the weight and give strength to run.

facts.statement: Researcher Busbey suggested that Langstonia's high skull implied a hunting strategy of producing quick cuts to weaken prey through bleeding, similar to Komodo dragons, rather than holding pressure indefinitely.
facts.quote: Busbey suggested the fact that his skull was high implied that these animals seek not to make pressure during the bite indefinitely, but to produce cuts then back quickly so that the bleeding weakens their prey slowly up to devour, similar to what has been thought to be the case for the extant Komodo dragon, thereby adopting a strategy of stalking in areas where prey transit frequently.

facts.statement: Langstonia was likely a terrestrial apex predator in its ecosystem, outcompeting large mammalian predators and predatory birds of the time.
facts.quote: these sebecids were probably the terrestrial apex predators in its ecosystem.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence indicates Langstonia lived in a warm, humid climate with heavy rainfall and short droughts (3-4 months), inhabiting watersheds, forests, and open grasslands.
facts.quote: The fossils found of other species - big fishes, manatees, large browsing meridiungulates as Granastrapotherium and Huilatherium, and some grazers as Pericotoxodon - indicate that the climate was warm and humid with heavy rainfall and with drought periods not extending beyond 3–4 months, consisting of watersheds, forests and certain adjacent areas of open grasslands where it could hunt down a large variety of species belonging to the megafauna.

facts.statement: Langstonia is classified within Sebecosuchia, a lineage of ziphodont terrestrial crocodylomorphs from the southern continent of Gondwana.
facts.quote: Langstonia is considered part of Sebecosuchia, a lineage of ziphodont terrestrial crocodylomorphs forming part of a separate lineage of the southern continent of Gondwana.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Langstonia in a clade within Sebecidae next to Sebecus icaeorhinus and Zulmasuchus, distinct from Barinasuchus and Bretesuchus.
facts.quote: As noted earlier, this species formerly part of the genus Sebecus and phylogenetic analyzes have consistently shown that these forms a clade within Sebecidae next to S. icaeorhinus and Zulmasuchus, not so closely related to Barinasuchus and Bretesuchus.

facts.statement: The name Langstonia honors the American paleontologist Wann Langston, Jr., and the genus lived during the Middle Miocene (Laventense age) in northern South America.
facts.quote: Langstonia (nombre que significa "[cocodrilo de] Langston" en honor del paleontólogo estadounidense Wann Langston, Jr.) es un género extinto de crocodilomorfo notosuquio perteneciente a la familia de los sebécidos que vivió durante el Mioceno medio (específicamente durante la edad-mamífero del Laventense) en el norte de América del Sur.

facts.statement: The genus Langstonia was established by Paolillo and Linares in 2007.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Paolillo & Linares, 2007

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Langstonia huilensis, originally described by Langston in 1965.
facts.quote: subdivision: * Langstonia huilensis Langston, 1965 (especie tipo)

facts.statement: Langstonia huilensis was previously misclassified as Sebecus huilensis and Sebecosuchus huilensis due to errors.
facts.quote: synonyms: * Sebecus huilensis Langston, 1965 Sebecosuchus huilensis Langston & Gasparini, 1997 (lapsus calami)

facts.statement: The specimens were formally described in 1965 by Wann Langston, Jr., who published a monograph on fossil crocodilians from Colombia.
facts.quote: La descripción de los especímenes de sebécido no llegaría sino hasta 1965, cuando el estadounidense Wann Langston, Jr. publicó su monografía Fossil Crocodylians from Colombia

facts.statement: Langston designated a fragment of the dentary bone, specimen UCMP 37877, as the holotype for the new species Sebecus huilensis.
facts.quote: En cuanto al material de sebécido, elige como holotipo de una nueva especie a un fragmento de hueso dentario, el espécimen UCMP 37877, a la cual denomina Sebecus huilensis

facts.statement: In 1977, Éric Buffetaut and Robert Hoffstetter reported a large partial cranial fragment (snout area) of this species from the Ipururo Formation in the Peruvian Amazon.
facts.quote: Posteriormente Éric Buffetaut y Robert Hoffstetter (1977) reportarían en la formación de Ipururo en la región amazónica de Perú la presencia de un enorme resto craneal parcial (área del hocico) a esta especie

facts.statement: Arthur Busbey reported new remains of the species from the Huila "Monkey Beds" in 1986, including a premaxilla fragment smaller than that of S. icaeorhinus.
facts.quote: Arthur Busbey (1986) más tarde reportaría nuevos restos de la especie también procedentes de la "capa de monos" de Huila en Colombia, esta vez un fragmento de premaxilar, más pequeño que el de S. icaeorhinus, e igualmente delgado

facts.statement: Wann Langston and Zulma Gasparini reported new remains of the species in 1997, including teeth, a premaxilla, a dentary fragment, and two vertebrae.
facts.quote: Langston, junto a la paleontóloga argentina Zulma Gasparini, volvería a reportar nuevos restos de la especie en una contribución sobre crocodilomorfos fósiles de Colombia para el volumen Vertebrate Paleontology of the Neotropics: The Miocene Fauna of La Venta (1997).

facts.statement: Alfredo Paolillo and Omar Linares described the large Miocene genus Barinasuchus from Venezuela in 2007.
facts.quote: Por otra parte, los venezolanos Alfredo Paolillo y Omar Linares (2007) describieron un nuevo género del Mioceno medio de gran tamaño, Barinasuchus de Venezuela.

facts.statement: Some authors, including Pol (2011, 2012) and Cavalho et al. (2010), still maintain both species within the genus Sebecus.
facts.quote: si bien algunos autores (Pol 2011, Pol 2012, Cavalho et al. 2010) aún mantienen a ambas especies dentro de Sebecus

facts.statement: The holotype dentary fragment is 68% larger than that of the Argentine species S. icaeorhinus and is proportionally thinner with more recurved and laterally compressed teeth.
facts.quote: el fragmento de dentario es 68% mayor que el de la especie argentina, S. icaeorhinus, y proporcionalmente más delgado, con dientes más recurvados y más comprimidos lateralmente

facts.statement: Busbey argued that the Peruvian fossil does not belong to S. huilensis due to its singular anatomy, featuring less spaced teeth and a wider snout.
facts.quote: Busbey asimismo descartaría la pertenencia del fósil peruano a S. huilensis, basándose en su anatomía singular, con dientes menos espaciados y un hocico más ancho.

facts.statement: Specimen UCMP 37877 is the anterior part of a right dentary preserving the mandibular symphysis with six dental alveoli, five of which contain broken teeth, collected in 1945.
facts.quote: UCMP 37877: La parte anterior de un hueso dentario derecho que preserva la sínfisis mandibular, con seis alvéolos dentales de los cuales cinco poseen dientes rotos, recolectados en 1945 en la localidad V-4517.

facts.statement: This element measures 189.0 millimeters in length, making it 68% larger than the holotype of Sebecus icaeorhinus.
facts.quote: Este elemento mide 189.0 milímetros de longitud, siendo 68% mayor que el espécimen tipo de Sebecus icaeorhinus.

facts.statement: Specimen UCMP 40186 is an elongated, thin, laterally compressed tooth with a slight curvature and larger serrations (3 per millimeter), whereas typical Langstonia serrations are 4 to 6 per millimeter.
facts.quote: UCMP 40186: Diente alargado, delgado y comprimido lateralmente, con una leve curvatura, intermedio en tamaño entre 44561 y el resto de dientes reportados, con sierras más grandes (3 por cada milímetro; en Langstonia típicamente son de 4 a 6 por milímetro).

facts.statement: Specimen UCMP 44561 is the largest reported dental crown fragment from La Venta, reaching 20.5 mm in height with a base width of 23.8 mm.
facts.quote: UCMP 44561: El mayor fragmento de corona dental reportado de La Venta, de la localidad V-4528. Alcanza hasta 20.5 mm de altura, pero su base es mucho más ancha que otros dientes, llegando a 23.8 mm.

facts.statement: This tooth is three times larger than the holotype teeth and is characterized by a blunt tip, relatively straight edges, an oval transverse profile, and small serrations.
facts.quote: Aparte de su tamaño, tres veces mayor que el de los dientes del holotipo de la especie, este diente se caracteriza por una punta roma, bordes relativamente rectos y un perfil tranverasal de forma más oval, con sierras pequeñas.

facts.statement: Specimen UCMP 44566 is the smallest tooth reported by Langston, measuring only 6.1 mm in base width, recovered from locality V-4421.
facts.quote: UCMP 44566: Es el menor de los dientes reportados por Langston (1965). Recuperado en la localidad V-4421, mide apenas 6.1 mm de anchura en la base.

facts.statement: Specimen TMM 41658-8 includes fragments of the left premaxilla, maxilla, splenial, suspensorium, quadratojugal, quadrate, opisthotic, squamosal, partial left jugal, partial left and right retroarticular processes, and an osteoderm fragment.
facts.quote: TMM 41658-8: Incluye un fragmento anterior del premaxilar izquierdo, un fragmento medio del maxilar izquierdo, un fragmento del hueso esplenial izquierdo, una parte posterior del hueso suspensorio izquierdo formado por partes del cuadratoyugal, el hueso cuadrado, el opistótico y el escamosal, un yugal parcial izquierdo, los procesos retroarticulares izquierdo y derecho (parciales) de la mandíbula y un fragmento de un osteodermo.

facts.statement: These fragments were recovered in 1976 from the "Monkey Pod" locality in La Venta by Dr. Ernest Lundelius Jr.
facts.quote: Estos fragmentos fueron recuperados en 1976 en la localidad "Monkey Pod" de La Venta (Miembro Baraya de la Formación Villavieja) por el dr. Ernest Lundelius Jr.

facts.statement: Specimen MUSM 912 is a single tooth found in the Arco Fitzcarrald area in the Peruvian Amazon at localities Inuya and Mapuya, with size and shape indistinguishable from L. huilensis.
facts.quote: MUSM 912: Un único diente hallado en el área del Arco Fitzcarrald en las localidades de Inuya y Mapuya en la zona amazónica de Perú; su tamaño y forma son indistinguibles de los de L. huilensis.

facts.statement: Langston considered the remains to be much more recent than the Argentine species S. icaeorhinus, suggesting a later time period.
facts.quote: Langston le da una nueva especie a los restos tomando en consideración que aparte de ser mucho más recientes, el fragmento de dentario es 68% mayor que el de la especie argentina, S. icaeorhinus, y proporcionalmente más delgado, con dientes más recurvados y más comprimidos lateralmente.

facts.statement: By naming Sebecus huilensis, Langston expanded the temporal range of the genus and family, which were previously known only from Eocene remains in Argentina.
facts.quote: En cuanto al material de sebécido, elige como holotipo de una nueva especie a un fragmento de hueso dentario, el espécimen UCMP 37877, a la cual denomina Sebecus huilensis; de esta manera amplía el rango temporal de este género y la propia familia, hasta entonces conocidos solo de restos del Eoceno de Argentina.

facts.statement: A partial cranial fragment of this species from the Ipururo Formation in Peru coincides in age with S. huilensis but differs by being larger and more robustly proportioned.
facts.quote: Posteriormente Éric Buffetaut y Robert Hoffstetter (1977) reportarían en la formación de Ipururo en la región amazónica de Perú la presencia de un enorme resto craneal parcial (área del hocico) a esta especie; si bien también coincide en edad con S. huilensis, se diferencia por su tamaño mayor y sus proporciones más robustas.

facts.statement: Paolillo and Linares assigned S. huilensis to the new genus Langstonia based on traits and temporal distribution, while S. querejazus was renamed Zulmasuchus.
facts.quote: Barinasuchus de Venezuela. En su artículo consideraron que los rasgos de dos de las especies de Sebecus, S. huilensis y S. querejazus del Paleoceno de Bolivia, además de su distribución temporal justifican la creación de géneros separados para ambos

facts.statement: A fossil from the Itaboraí Basin in Brazil dating to the Middle Paleocene has been classified as Sebecus cf. huilensis, suggesting a lineage with an extensive temporal and geographic record.
facts.quote: Finalmente, un fósil de un premaxilar y un fragmento de maxilar hallado en la cuenca de Itaboraí en Brasil que data del Paleoceno medio (y en donde se han hallado otros fósiles de sebécidos), ha sido clasificado como afín a esta especie, bajo el nombre de Sebecus cf. huilensis

facts.statement: Langston referred a series of ziphodont teeth found in the area to this species, along with similar teeth classified generally as Sebecus sp. from the Eocene in the Santander department.
facts.quote: Adicionalmente Langston refiere una serie de dientes zifodontes hallados en el área a esta especie, junto a algunos dientes que refiere como parecidos pero que clasifica de manera general a Sebecus sp., los cuales no proceden del Mioceno sino del Eoceno, hallados en el departamento de Santander, en Colombia.

facts.statement: It is debated whether both species should remain within the genus Sebecus, as some authors still maintain this classification.
facts.quote: si bien algunos autores (Pol 2011, Pol 2012, Cavalho et al. 2010) aún mantienen a ambas especies dentro de Sebecus

facts.statement: Fossils of Langstonia were found in the Itaboraí Basin in the state of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
facts.quote: MCT 1795-R / 1796-R: Consiste de material de sebécido hallado en la cuenca de Itaboraí en el estado de Río de Janeiro en Brasil.

facts.statement: The known fossil material includes a complete left premaxilla with a preserved tooth and a piece of the left maxilla with two tooth sockets.
facts.quote: Incluye un premaxilar izquierdo completo con un diente preservado, y una pieza del maxilar izquierdo con dos alvéolos.

facts.statement: Langstonia possessed ziphodont teeth that were flattened on the sides, slightly curved backward, serrated with 5 to 6 small denticles per millimeter, and lacked surface grooves.
facts.quote: Los dientes son del tipo zifodonte, muy aplanados en sus lados, ligeramente curvados hacia atrás y con los bordes aserrados con pequeños dentículos (entre 5 a 6 dentículos por cada milímetro en los dientes de este género) y además sin ningún tipo de surcos en su superficie.

facts.statement: The type fossil of Langstonia is larger than Sebecus icaeorhinus and has flatter jaws and teeth, implying a skull that was high and laterally flattened unlike the horizontally flattened skulls of modern crocodiles.
facts.quote: Como se mencionó anteriormente, el fósil tipo de la especie es de mayor tamaño que el de Sebecus icaeorhinus, con mandíbulas y dientes aún más aplanados, si bien sus proporciones generales recuerdan a esta especie, de lo que se deduce que su cráneo sería también alto y aplanado lateralmente, en contraste con los cocodrilos modernos, que poseen generalmente un cráneo aplanado horizontalmente y con dientes cónicos.

facts.statement: Langstonia lived in a warm, humid environment with river basins, forests, and open grasslands where it hunted various megafauna.
facts.quote: constituido por cuencas fluviales, selvas y algunas zonas contiguas de pastizales abiertos en donde podría cazar a una gran variedad de megafauna.

facts.statement: Langstonia is classified as part of Sebecosuchia, a lineage of terrestrial ziphodont crocodylomorphs from the ancient southern continent of Gondwana.
facts.quote: Langstonia es considerado como parte de Sebecosuchia, el linaje de crocodilomorfos terrestres zifodontes que forma parte de un linaje propio del antiguo continente meridional de Gondwana.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses consistently place Langstonia in a clade within Sebecidae alongside Sebecus icaeorhinus and Zulmasuchus, separate from Barinasuchus and Bretesuchus.
facts.quote: Como se ha señalado antes, esta especie antes formaba parte del género Sebecus y los análisis filogenéticos han mostrado consistentemente que forma un clado dentro de Sebecidae junto a S. icaeorhinus y a Zulmasuchus, apartado de Barinasuchus y Bretesuchus.

facts.statement: Langstonia lived between 21 and 17.5 million years ago during the Aquitanian to Burdigalian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Aquitanian to Burdigalian (21 to 17.5 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The 1997 report included new specimens of teeth, a premaxilla, a dentary fragment, and sacral and caudal vertebrae.
rejected.quote: In this case it would be new specimens of teeth, a somewhat fuller premaxilla, an anterior fragment of dentary, and two vertebrae: a sacral and a caudal

rejected.statement: Specimens from the 1997 discovery are deposited in the Geological Museum of Ingeominas.
rejected.quote: The specimens discovered on this occasion were deposited in the Geological Museum of Ingeominas

rejected.statement: An associated sacral vertebra measured 10.7 cm high by 5.5 cm wide with a wide, rectangular neural spine, and its sacral ribs are estimated to be 10 cm wide at the rear end.
rejected.quote: The associated vertebrae are an amphycoelian sacral with a sacral rib attached, with a wide, rectangular neural spine; it measured 10.7 cm high by 5.5 cm wide, while it is estimated that the sacral ribs should be 10 cm wide at its rear end.
